summary: Samuel Wells Williams (1812–1884) was a scholar in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1831–1832) and held a post at Yale University from circa 1877 to 1884.

Sandra A. Wawrytko works in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She taught Michael J. Tetreault and held posts at San Diego State University, where she is attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.
Sandra Bell is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and also held an academic post there.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where she studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and teacher Anne MacDonald.

Sang-Kyun Sun works in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Sanghasen Singh (attested 1995) and served as a lecturer at JinGak Sangha College (attested 1995).

Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tengtho Monastery and the Institute of Language and Culture Studies, taught at Simtokha Dzong, and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (attested 1999–2004).

Sangharakshita (1925–2018) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Dhardo Rinpoche, Jianmin Chen, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dudjom Rinpoche, later founding the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

Sangseraima Ujeed (b. 1988) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2017) and held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at UC Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

Sanjay Subrahmanyam (b. 1961) is a historian who studied at Delhi School of Economics and University of Delhi. He held chairs at Oxford, the EHESS, UCLA (also serving as founding director 2005–2011), and the Collège de France (2013).
Sanjaya Lall (1940–2005) studied at St. Xavier's High School, Patna, and at St John's College, Oxford (~1960–1965). He held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1970 to 2005.
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya (attested 1994) and traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta (b. 1931), a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht under Jan Gonda. She held posts at Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, Jadavpur, Utrecht (~1970–1986), and Oxford (~1986–2000).
Sanne Dokter-Mersch (b. 1989) is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

Sao Htun Hmat Win was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard and under Bhaddanta Narada. He taught at Rangoon University, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs (attested 2002).

Saphalya Amatya is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Chief Exploration Officer at the Department of Archaeology (attested 1974) and as Editor of Ancient Nepal (attested 1987).

Sara L. McClintock works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She earned a PhD from Harvard (-2002) under Tom Tillemans, was a professor at UW–Madison (attested 2003), and became associate professor of religion at Emory University.

Sarah Aoife Richardson specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (-2016) under Jenny Purtle, having also studied under scholars including John C. and Susan L. Huntington.

Sarah E. Fraser works in history, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, and she held posts as Associate Professor at Northwestern University (1996) and Directrice d'Études at EPHE (2000).

Sarah H. Jacoby specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Yale University (~1995–1999) and the University of Virginia (~2000–2007), holding posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (2009).

Sarah Harding (b. 1951) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Drubpön Lama Tenpa, served as a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation (~2000), and held a post at Naropa University (~1992–2018).
